# Notification

Notification markup, configuration, behavior, and usage example. A persistent, manually-dismissed panel of messages. Author only notificationBell, a plain button: there can be as many as the page needs, and every one of them opens and closes the same single panel. pgs.notification builds that panel, a modal (see Modal), the first time a notification arrives or a bell is clicked, so nothing else is written on the page. Opening any other dialog on the page (e.g. the mobile menu) closes it automatically, and vice versa. With no notificationBell on the page the notifications are still kept, but nothing can open the panel, so an error is written to the console. Split from Toast, which is ephemeral and auto-dismissing. Both are the shared alert card underneath (see Alerts): this component only manages the group around it. Full JSON field list is under @pgs-data "notification"; full JS options list is under each @api method below. The JSON form and the JS options now use the same names; the previous message and title-close keys are still accepted as aliases. Two custom events are dispatched, owned by the shared alert engine (see Alerts): pgs:alert:buttonClick on a buttons[] element when clicked (detail: id, buttonId, type, title, description, link; cancelable — call event.preventDefault() to stop a link's navigation and finish async work first), and pgs:alert:close on a notification element right before it is removed, whether by its own dismiss button or by deleteAll() below (detail: id, type, title, description).

## PGS

- `notificationLoad`: creates one or more notifications from comma-separated JSON objects on page load; see @pgs-data "notification" for every accepted field.
- `notificationBell`: a plain button that opens and closes the notification panel each time it is clicked. The JavaScript gives it aria-haspopup and keeps aria-expanded in step with the panel, for every bell on the page.
- `notificationBell-counter`: write one yourself, bare like this, inside notificationBell to place it yourself; the module leaves it alone and never generates a second one.

## PGS generated by JavaScript

- `_notificationBell-counter`: appended inside notificationBell when no notificationBell-counter was written by hand. Either form displays the current count of _alert elements inside the panel.
- `_notificationsDialog`: identifies the dialog generated to hold the notification panel, inside the one modal built for all the bells.
- `_notifications`: the scrollable list of notifications, created inside that dialog together with it.
- `_notifications-close`: the button generated at the top of that list, above the first notification, which closes the panel; its label is the internal panelCloseTitle default. It also carries _modal-close, Modal's own generated form of the close control it hands off to.
- `_notifications-empty`: shown inside the panel whenever it holds no notifications; its text comes from the internal emptyMessage default.

## PGS Data

- `notification`: JSON object (or several, comma-separated) read by notificationLoad on page load — every field, with its accepted values and its default, is annotated in the reference below.

## JavaScript API

- `pgs.notification.init(root)`: scans root for notificationLoad and initializes them (including the bell counter); runs automatically on page load and again via pgs.init(root) for content added later. Opening/closing the dialog itself is handled by pgs.modal (see Modal).
- `pgs.notification.trigger(root)`: alias of pgs.notification.init(root).
- `pgs.notification.error(optionsOrTitle)`: a title string, or an options object — see the full field reference in the commented example below.
- `pgs.notification.success(optionsOrTitle)`: a title string, or an options object — see the full field reference in the commented example below.
- `pgs.notification.info(optionsOrTitle)`: a title string, or an options object — see the full field reference in the commented example below.
- `pgs.notification.warning(optionsOrTitle)`: a title string, or an options object — see the full field reference in the commented example below.
- `pgs.notification.neutral(optionsOrTitle)`: the plain notification, same arguments as the others; it has no title or glyph of its own, so pass at least a description.
- `pgs.notification.deleteAll()`: closes every notification in the panel by calling each one's own close, the same as clicking its dismiss button — so each still dispatches its own pgs:alert:close.

## Related elements

### PGS

- `flex`: provides the flex layout; direction and spacing are flags in its bracket.
- `hidden`: keeps every notificationLoad out of the layout, since it only carries a payload.
- `button`: uses the related button component or utility in this example.
- `icon`: draws the glyph that marks the notification type; see Icon for the whole set.

### PGS Options (component brackets)

- `column`: stacks the examples vertically.
- `gapTexts`: spaces the content inside each example.
- `btnIconOnly`: presents notificationBell, and the generated dismiss button, as icon buttons.
- `icon-bell`: the glyph on the control that opens the panel.

### Other

- `alerts`: owns the card itself and the engine that builds it (icon, content, dismiss button, action buttons, events — see its own @pgs-generated for every _alert* token); this component only manages the panel, the bell and the stacking list around it.
- `neutral`: the plain severity option owned by Alerts; no colour, no glyph and no title of its own, so the card stays on the box surface.
- `success`: the success severity option owned by Alerts.
- `error`: the error severity option owned by Alerts.
- `warning`: the warning severity option owned by Alerts.
- `info`: the info severity option owned by Alerts.
- `gapSections`: separates the examples.
- `btnTransparent`: the appearance the component gives the buttons passed in the payload; see Button.
- `modal`: the one modal pgs.notification builds around the panel; it provides the open/close/toggle behavior shared with every other dialog on the page.
- `modal-dialog-content`: identifies the JS-generated styled content area inside the dialog, wrapping notifications.
- `btnMini`: keeps the generated panel-close button small; see Button.
- `dialogRight`: slides the notification dialog in from the right; see Modal for other positions.
- `icon-circleXmark`: the glyph of the error type.
- `icon-circleCheck`: the glyph of the success type.
- `icon-circleInfo`: the glyph of the info type.
- `icon-triangleExclamation`: the glyph of the warning type.
- `icon-close`: the cross the dismiss button draws.

## Output

Complete HTML markup and usage example for Notification.

## PGS Data fields

```html
pgs-data='notification[{
    "id": null,                  // string; generated when omitted, and reported by every event
    "title": "",                 // omitted falls back to the title of the type
    "description": "",           // plain text under the title
    "type": "info",              // neutral | error | success | warning | info
    "icon": null,                // HTML string; null uses the icon of the type
    "closeTitle": "Close",       // accessible name of the dismiss button, which always draws a cross
    "buttons": [                 // omitted or empty leaves only the dismiss button
        {
            "id": null,          // reported as buttonId by pgs:alert:buttonClick
            "title": "",         // label of the button
            "link": null,        // navigates there; omit it to only dispatch the event
            "close": true,       // dismisses the notification after the click
            "optionButton": null // pgs-data token added to the button, e.g. btnMini
        }
    ]
}]'
```


## JavaScript Usage

```js
pgs.notification.success({
    id: undefined,
    title: "",
    description: "",
    icon: null,
    closeTitle: "Close",
    buttons: [
        { id: undefined, title: "", link: undefined, close: true, optionButton: undefined }
    ]
});
```

## Examples

### Bell

The control that opens and closes the panel, and the only markup this component needs on the page. It is a plain button: pgs.notification builds the counter inside it, and the panel itself the first time it is needed.

```html
<button type="button" pgs="button['btnIconOnly'] notificationBell" aria-label="Open notifications">
    <i pgs="icon['icon-bell']"></i>
</button>
```

### Several bells

Put as many as the page needs, in the header, in a menu, in a footer: they all open the same panel and show the same count.

```html
<button type="button" pgs="button notificationBell">Notifications</button>
```

### Neutral

A message with nothing to signal: no severity colour, no glyph, and the title left out so only the text shows.

```html
<div pgs="hidden notificationLoad" pgs-data='notification[{
    "title": "Hi!",
    "description": "The report you asked for is ready.",
    "type": "neutral",
    "icon": "<img src=\"../assets/img/logo.svg\" alt=\"\">"
}]'></div>
```

### Success

A completed operation. The element is hidden and consumed on load: the notification it describes is moved into the panel.

```html
<div pgs="hidden notificationLoad" pgs-data='notification[{
        "title": "Profile approved",
        "description": "Your profile has been reviewed and approved.",
        "type": "success",
        "icon": null
    }]'></div>
```

### Error

A failure the user has to know about, with a button to try the operation again.

```html
<div pgs="hidden notificationLoad" pgs-data='notification[{
        "title": "Something went wrong",
        "description": "Please try again later.",
        "type": "error",
        "icon": null,
        "buttons": [{ "title": "Retry", "link": "#" }]
    }]'></div>
```

### Warning

Something is missing but nothing is broken, so the button leads to where it can be completed.

```html
<div pgs="hidden notificationLoad" pgs-data='notification[{
        "title": "Your profile is incomplete",
        "description": "Complete your profile to unlock all features.",
        "type": "warning",
        "icon": null,
        "buttons": [{ "title": "Complete profile", "link": "#" }]
    }]'></div>
```

### Info with several buttons

Buttons carrying an id instead of a link dispatch pgs:alert:buttonClick with that id, which is how a question is answered without leaving the page.

```html
<div pgs="hidden notificationLoad" pgs-data='notification[{
        "title": "Are you enjoying the portal?",
        "description": "Your feedback helps us improve.",
        "type": "info",
        "icon": null,
        "buttons": [
            { "id": "yes", "title": "Yes" },
            { "id": "no", "title": "No" }
        ]
    }]'></div>
```
